title: Find a yearly growth rate by testing a round guess, not by dividing the total growth by the years
description: Growth rates over several years: a quick way to do this case calculation in your head, with a worked example.
hook: Growth questions ask how big something will be after a few years. You can get very close without compound interest formulas.
body:
The problem

Revenue: $100M → $121M in 2 years. Growth per year?

Step by step

  1. +21% total: don't just halve it
  2. 1.1 × 1.1
  3. = 1.21 ✓

Answer: 10% a year.

How to say it in the interview

Revenue grew from one hundred million to one hundred and twenty one million in two years. What was the growth each year?

Total growth is twenty one percent, but it compounds, so do not just halve it.

Try ten percent: one point one times one point one.

That is one point two one. A match.

So growth was ten percent a year.

Guess a round rate, test it, and adjust. Interviewers love seeing the check.

Notice that the last step is always about meaning. A number on its own earns half the marks; a number with "so what" earns all of them.
outro: Small things like this add up. Try it in your next practice case and notice how it changes the conversation. Practise sums like this in the free case maths drill.
